$comment: Shared corpus for Smalltalk literal/comment scanning. Read by BOTH client/src/__tests__/smalltalkScan.test.ts and server/src/lexer/__tests__/lexerCorpusAgreement.test.ts so the two workspaces cannot drift apart. Add a case here and both sides must handle it.

cases.name: character literal quoting a string delimiter
cases.why: the issue-466 bug: `$'` read as a string opener swallowed the rest of the file

cases.name: character literal quoting a comment delimiter
cases.why: `$"` opens no comment

cases.name: character literal quoting a block delimiter
cases.why: `$[` opens no block, so it must not raise a bracket depth counter

cases.name: character literal quoting a statement separator
cases.why: `$.` ends no statement — the step-point scan must keep going to find `with:`

cases.name: character literal quoting a dollar
cases.why: the escape character is itself quotable; only ONE character is consumed

cases.name: character literal quoting a space
cases.why: `$ ` is a legal space literal; the `.` after it still ends the statement

cases.name: character literal truncated at end of input
cases.why: a trailing `$` must not read past the end of the buffer

cases.name: string with a doubled-quote escape
cases.why: `''` inside a string is an escaped quote, not a close followed by an open

cases.name: string containing a comment delimiter
cases.why: a double quote inside a string opens no comment

cases.name: comment containing a string delimiter
cases.why: an apostrophe inside a comment opens no string — the two must be tracked in one pass

cases.name: comment containing a character literal
cases.why: inside a comment the `$` is prose, not a literal; the comment is consumed whole

cases.name: string containing a character literal
cases.why: inside a string the `$` is data; the string is consumed whole

cases.name: string spanning lines
cases.why: the scan carries string state across a newline

cases.name: comment spanning lines
cases.why: the scan carries comment state across a newline

cases.name: empty string and empty comment
cases.why: a zero-length body must still consume both delimiters

cases.name: string immediately followed by another string
cases.why: the close of one literal must not be read as the open of the next

cases.name: symbol with a quoted body
cases.why: the client scanners treat `#` as an ordinary token character and consume only the quoted part; the lexer emits `#'...'` as one Symbol token. Both land in the same place, which is all that matters for depth and statement-end decisions.

cases.name: comment with a doubled-quote escape
cases.why: a comment escapes its own delimiter by doubling it, exactly as a string does; the class comments under gs-src/refactoring/ are written this way

cases.name: comment ending in an escaped quote
cases.why: the escape run sits right against the closing delimiter, where an off-by-one splits the comment into several tokens and the formatter emits only the first

cases.name: string with a doubled-quote escape run
cases.why: two escapes in a row must not be read as a close followed by an open
